target_customer: Consumers, mostly women, who buy personalized skincare by subscription after a skin quiz
problem: Generic skincare products do not fit individual skin. Proven builds custom formulas from a database of skin, ingredient and product data.
business_model: Direct-to-consumer subscription and e-commerce, plus retail and Amazon lines

founders.name: Amy Yuan
prior_employers: AI-powered personalization company she co-founded and scaled to over 150 million dollars total revenue (name not given)
previous_startups: AI-powered personalization company (unnamed on the company site)
founders.background_notes: Per the YC company page. Built the Skin Genome Project.

founders.name: Ming Zhao
founders.background_notes: Appeared on Shark Tank season 11 in 2020 seeking 500 thousand dollars for 5 percent and left without a deal.

competitors.name: Curology
competitors.what: Personalized prescription skincare delivered by subscription
competitors.funding_then: 15 million dollars Series B in Aug 2016 and 4.2 million in 2015

technical_complexity.rationale: Needed a data model across skin, ingredients and products, plus formulation and custom manufacturing. A data-driven consumer goods build, with some hard parts in supply chain.

defensibility.rationale: The Skin Genome database is proprietary and the company has patents, but customers can switch skincare brands easily and BoldIP notes patent questions.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Function of Beauty acquired Atolla in 2021; no source shows an incumbent buying Proven. Proven acquired the fragrance brand Noteworthy in 2022 for about 650 thousand dollars.

market_need_then: Rising demand for customized beauty and DTC skincare in 2018, with personalization brands such as Curology already funded.

branding.domain_note: Consumer site provenskincare.com; the company group name Proven Group is distinct.

identity.visual_style: Clean clinical beauty site built around a skin quiz
identity.voice_and_tone: Scientific and data-led claims such as the Skin Genome Project

branding.brand_signature: Skin Genome Project and AI personalization claim
branding.community_and_virality: Shark Tank appearance in May 2020 and Instagram, TikTok and Facebook accounts; the MIT AI Technology of the Year claim is company reported.

brand_strength.rationale: Shark Tank exposure, press coverage and a distinct science story, but the name is a generic word and sales reportedly fell about 5.5 percent to nearly 35 million dollars per one listing.

outcome_analysis: Proven is still operating with about 40 staff. It raised a 6 million seed, a Reg A+ offering of about 3 million, and a 12.2 million Series A in September 2023 from existing investors after reaching break-even, according to company statements. It added Noteworthy fragrance and Amazon lines, but one listing says sales dipped to nearly 35 million dollars, so the outcome is a modest sustained consumer brand rather than a breakout.
notes: Seed date not stated in the cited article. Reg A+ amount is about 3 million per Retail Dive and almost 2.7 million gross per another search result; the offering was announced in October 2021 as up to 60 million. Total raised conflicts across aggregators (CB Insights 12.32M, Caplight 21.32M, Standout 23.3M). A fan site claims a 2019 Unilever acquisition, which conflicts with all other sources and is treated as false. Curology competitor source is dated 2016, before the batch. Zhao's education and employers not found in sources opened.
